National Weather Service Greenville-Spartanburg SC
614 AM EST Fri Nov 20 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Rain chances have increased late Saturday through early Sunday for 
the eastern half of our forecast area and for most of our area during
the middle of next week.

Updated the aviation discussion for the 12Z TAFs.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1. Dry through at least early Saturday with above normal
temperatures expected through Monday.
2. Piedmont rain chances increase over the weekend in association
with a coastal low, but forecast confidence remains fairly
low. Considerably colder temperatures and possible frozen
precipitation in NC mountains by the middle of next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Key message 1: Dry through at least early Saturday with above normal
temperatures expected through Monday.

The large-scale upper level pattern will remain amplified through 
the weekend, with the upper ridge axis drifting eastward and off 
the Atlantic Coast over the weekend. This will allow broad sfc high 
pressure to linger to our north, but gradually weaken over our area 
over the next few days. Temperatures will continue to warm under 
slowly rising heights with highs fcst to approach/reach 70 degrees 
across most of our lower terrain today. Highs will likely be about
4 to 8 degrees cooler on Saturday due to increased cloud cover and
stronger NELY winds. 

In addition, lingering dry air is expected to produce critical RH 
values again this aftn/evening, especially over the NC mountains. 
Fortunately, winds should be fairly light over the mountains. 
Nonetheless, wildfire danger will be somewhat elevated today.


Key message 2: Piedmont rain chances increase over the weekend in
association with a coastal low, but forecast confidence remains
fairly low. Considerably colder temperatures and possible frozen 
precipitation in NC mountains by the middle of next week.

A weak upper low is expected to organize into a subtropical low 
over the Florida/Southeast Coast later tonight and over the weekend. 
The deterministic global models continue to struggle with run-to-run 
consistency regarding the location of cyclone development and its 
track. The most recent runs of these models now have the low deve-
loping along the Florida/Southeast Coast and track it northward over 
the weekend and into Monday. This trend will increase rain chances 
for mainly the eastern part of our CWA late Saturday into Sunday. 
A weak upper shortwave and an associated cold front approaching 
from the west will increase rain chances mainly in the NC mtns on 
Monday, but any QPF should be minimal. In the wake of the cold 
front, temperatures will cool considerably on Tues and Wed. At 
the same time, another low is progged to spin up somewhere off 
the Southeast Coast while robust surface high pressure lingers 
to our north. The interaction of these synoptic features will 
increase our precip chances again by the middle of next week
and could produce some frozen precip over the NC mtns. Quite
a bit of uncertainty remains wrt how this pattern will pan out
next week, but it looks like we have a decent chance of getting 
some widespread precip across most of our area.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
At KCLT and elsewhere: Dry and VFR through the 12Z TAF period. 
Seeing mostly BKN VFR cirrus across the terminals this morning. 
Cloud cover may scatter out from mid-morning to late afternoon 
before going BKN to OVC this evening into tonight. Winds east of the 
mountains will toggle more NE by mid-morning but KHKY should see 
calm to light NNW/NW winds through this morning before toggling more 
NE by early afternoon. KAVL will remain calm this morning before 
picking up out of the E/ESE by early afternoon. Winds will go calm 
again at KAVL this evening into tonight. Wind speeds will gradually 
increase for east of the mountains towards the end of the TAF 
period. Low-end gusts will develop early Saturday morning for most 
locations east of the mountains. However, gusts are not expected at 
KHKY and KCLT should not see gusts develop until late Saturday 
morning. 

Outlook: A developing coastal low may bring rain and associated 
restrictions late Saturday into early Sunday for terminals east of 
the mountains but confidence remains low. A cold front may bring 
rain chances back along the NC/TN border Monday before better rain 
chances, and possible restrictions, return area-wide by mid-week.
